title: Functional assessment of lysosomal Rab7 and RILP with RNA interference and overexpression in Spodoptera frugiperda Sf9 cell lines
protocol: Check the restriction endonuclease cleavage sites on nucleotide sequences and PIZT plasmid.
Prepare the PCR reaction master mix, which includes sequence-containing plasmids, primers, master mix with proofreading polymerase, and ddH2O.
Perform PCR amplification according to specified cycling conditions.
Prepare 1.5% agarose gel.
Load samples and DL2000 DNA marker onto the agarose gel.
Carry out electrophoresis at 80 V with TAE running buffer on the HE-120 horizontal electrophoresis tank until loading dye has progressed 2/3 down the gel (about 30 min).
Place the gel on a TGreen transilluminator or equivalent long wave ultraviolet illuminator.
Pick out related lanes with a surgical knife.
Recover fragments following the instructions of a Universal DNA Purification Kit or an equivalent kit.
Store recovered fragments at −20°C for several weeks.
Insert fragments into a T-Vector pMD19 using a DNA Ligation Kit.
Add 100 μL competent cells to 10 μL ligation mixture and keep on ice for 30 min.
Place tubes at 42°C for 90 s using a thermo cell or water bath.
Add 1 mL LB culture medium to the mixture and culture at 37°C, 150 rpm for 1 h.
Spread 100 μL bacteria on LB plates containing 0.1 g/L ampicillin.
Culture bacteria at 37°C until colonies appear.
Spread bacteria on LB agar plates containing ampicillin and X-gal for blue/white screening.
Pick white colonies with recombinant plasmid.
Culture selected bacteria in 1 mL LB culture medium for at least 4 hours.
Perform PCR using universal primers M13F(-47)/RV-M on cultured bacteria.
Sequence DNA samples in a biotech company.
Compare sequences with DNAMAN software.
Extract plasmids from corrected colonies following the TIANprep Mini Plasmid Kit instructions.
Store correct vectors at −20°C for long-term storage.
Supply correct fragments to FastDigest system containing EcoRI, XbaI, and FastDigest Green buffer.
Incubate FastDigest system in a thermo cell at 37°C for 1 hour.
Perform agarose gel electrophoresis on the digested fragments.
Recover DNA fragments from agarose gel.
Apply recovered DNA fragments for DNA ligation using T4 DNA Ligase according to the user manual.
Combine 0.3 μL T4 DNA ligase, 1 μL 10× T4 DNA Ligase Buffer, 5–6 μL sequence fragments, and 3–4 μL plasmid fragment in a reaction system.
Incubate the ligation system at 16°C for at least 1 hour.
Transfect the ligation systems into DH5α chemically competent cells.
Culture positive colonies in LB medium supplemented with Zeocin.
Extract plasmids from correct colonies using E.Z.N.A. Endo-Free Plasmid Mini Kit II instructions.
Store endo-free plasmids at -20°C.
Add T7 RNA polymerase promoter to gene sequences with PCR by including the T7 promoter sequence at the 5′-end of either of the amplification primers.
Prepare the PCR reaction master mix and perform the cloning.
Mix 5-10 cycles at an annealing temperature approximately 5°C above the melting temperature of the gene-specific sequences.
Follow with 20-35 cycles of annealing approximately 5°C above the melting temperature of the entire primer, including the T7 promoter.
Examine PCR products by agarose gel electrophoresis to collect target fragments.
Clone the fragments into recommended pGEM-T or pGEM-T Easy Vectors.
Transfect constructs into DH5α chemically competent cells.
Verify positive colonies and culture correct colonies.
Extract and purify plasmids to obtain high-quality DNA templates.
Linearize DNA by digestion with restriction endonuclease, for example, EcoRI.
Supply linearized DNA with the T7 reaction system to produce single-stranded transcripts.
Incubate at 37°C for up to 2-6 hours to maximize yield.
Mix equal volumes of complementary RNA reactions to anneal RNA strands.
Incubate at 70°C for 10 minutes.
Slowly cool double-stranded RNA to room temperature.
Add 1 μL freshly diluted RNase Solution and 1 μL RQ1 RNase-Free DNase per 20 μL reaction volume.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Add 0.1 volume of 3M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) to the mixture.
Add 1 volume of isopropanol or 2.5 volumes of 95% ethanol and mix.
Place on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge at top speed for 10 min.
Wash the pellet with 0.5 mL of cold 70% ethanol.
Air-dry the pellet.
Resuspend the RNA sample in 40–100 μL nuclease-free water.
Transfect overexpression plasmids and dsRNA into cultured Sf9 cells separately.
Cultivate and operate cells in a sterile environment.
Gently flush attached Sf9 cells with cell culture medium to make a suspension (approximately 10^5 cells).
Carefully place 25 mm coverslips on the wells of 6-well plates and add 1.5 mL cell suspension per well.
Remove bubbles between plate and coverslips.
Seal the plates with sealing film and place in a cell incubator at 28°C for 6–8 h.
Transfect cells using FuGENE HD Transfection Reagent following the technical manuals.
Incubate the mixture for 10–15 min at room temperature (about 25°C).
Add 50 μL of the transfection mixture per well in a 6-well plate and gently mix.
Place the plates into an incubator.
After 24 h, add 0.05 mM Harmine to the treatment group and DMSO to the control group.
Harvest cells after cell transfection for 24–48 h.
Extract total RNA using TRNzol universal reagent following the instructions.
Examine RNA quality with NanoDrop spectrophotometer.
Synthesize cDNA using a FastKing RT Kit (with gDNase) according to the procedure.
Perform qRT-PCR with a CFX Connect Real-Time System and SYBR Green Realtime PCR Master Mix.
Gently remove the culture medium from cell slides.
Wash cell slides three times with PBS buffer.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde for 10–15 minutes.
Penetrate cells with PBS containing 1% Tween 80 for 10 minutes.
Block cells with blocking buffer for 1 hour.
Dilute Sf-Atg8 polyclonal antibody (1:1000) and Sf-Cathepsin L polyclonal antibody (1:1000) in blocking buffer.
Incubate cell slides with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer at room temperature for 2 hours.
Wash cell slides with PBS for 3 times.
Dilute CY3 Conjugated AffiniPure Goat Anti-Mouse IgG and CY3 Conjugated AffiniPure Goat Anti-Rabbit IgG in PBS to a ratio of 1:1000 each.
Add 1 mL of diluted secondary antibodies per well.
Incubate the slides with secondary antibodies in the dark at room temperature (about 25°C) for 2 h.
Dilute CY3 Conjugated AffiniPure Goat Anti-Mouse IgG and FITC Conjugated AffiniPure Goat Anti-Rabbit IgG in PBS to a ratio of 1:1000 and 1:500, respectively.
Add 1 mL of diluted secondary antibodies per well for RNAi.
Incubate the slides with secondary antibodies in the dark at room temperature (about 25°C) for 2 h.
Dilute Hoechst 33258 in PBS to a ratio between 1:3,000 and 1:5,000.
Add 1 mL of diluted Hoechst 33258 per well.
Incubate the slides with Hoechst 33258 in the dark at room temperature (about 25°C) for 10 min.
Wash coverslips with PBS buffer for 3 times.
Add a small drop of fluorescent mounting media on glass slides.
Place coverslips upside down on the drop of mounting media and seal with varnish.
Air-dry the prepared samples in the dark at room temperature (about 25°C) before observation.
Observe the overexpression results with a laser confocal microscope.
Carry out the fluorescence analysis using NIS-Elements BR software.
Use DAPI 405 nm to detect blue fluorescence (425–475 nm).
Use FITC 488 nm to detect green fluorescence (500–550 nm).
Use TRITC 561 nm to detect red fluorescence (570–620 nm).
Apply a Plan Apo VC 20×/0.75 DIC N2 objective lens.
Adjust the zoom to 2.
Set scan resolution to 512 pixels.
Set capture resolution to 2048 pixels.
Obtain a final 3 × 12-bit figure focusing on GFP-positive cells.
Take at least five fluorescence pictures under fixed parameters for each treatment.
Carry out more than twice biological replications during overexpression experiments.
Check the results of RNAi assay with a fluorescence microscope.
Carry out the fluorescence analysis using Image-Pro Plus 6.0 software.
Use a fluorescence microscope or laser confocal microscope for analysis.
Choose five visual fields for taking pictures under fixed parameters for each treatment.
Perform biological replications more than twice.
Analyze GFP-positive cells in overexpression images using NIS-Elements BR software.
Open captured confocal figures on the software for further analysis.
Turn to the FITC view.
Select the “Binary” option.
Set parameters: intensity from 50 to 4,000, smooth 2.
Copy the Binary selection to ROI (Region of Interest).
Select options for detection including ROI area, mean intensity, mean red, mean green, and mean blue.
Measure the ROI data.
Export the statistics of the ROI to Excel.
Open figures in Image-Pro Plus software.
Perform Edit - Convert to - Gray Scale 8.
Choose Enhance - Invert Contrast.
Measure optical density using calibrated settings.
Select New and Std Optical Density in the popup window.
Set incident level in Options and apply to all figures.
Choose density ranges for red fluorescence ≥15 and green fluorescence ≥20.
Evaluate area, diameter (mean), density (mean), and IOD.
Set area threshold ≥20 to exclude impurities.
Count and save statistical data.
Analyze data with SPSS 22.0 using t-test for two groups comparison.
Perform one-way ANOVA followed by Duncan’s multiple range tests for treatment comparisons.
Generate figures with NIS-Elements Viewer 5.21.
Create graphs with GraphPad Prism 8.0 following tutorials and guides.
